# Hidden author ground truth: status-page
DO NOT expose this file to either audit variant. Authored from raw source and official docs, without reading cfdoctor or previous eval fixtures.
Pin: eidam/cf-workers-status-page@f5b49dcae71e12c613b8f00094ed16b735925f64.
Scope: scheduled monitoring and KV persistence, notification helpers, monthly cleanup CLI. UI only supplies persistence-consumer context.
All conclusions are static source proofs / hypothetical schedules, not runtime reproduction or claims about the project's deployed service.

## Significant confirmed defects
S1 (P1/P2, primary): A rejected health-check fetch aborts the whole monitoring run, leaving previous healthy state in KV.
Evidence: src/functions/cronTrigger.js:55 awaits fetch without per-monitor try/catch; state is written only at :156 after the entire for-loop. index.js:31 correctly keeps the whole promise alive but does not recover failures.
Proof schedule: previous KV says all 3 monitors healthy; location lookup and KV read succeed; monitor 1 fetch rejects (DNS/TLS/network failure). Its status is never recorded, monitors 2 and 3 never checked, lastUpdate time and KV write never reached: zero new state writes. If monitor 2 fails instead, monitor 1's in-memory change is also lost. HTTP 500 is a different path: fetch resolves, expected-status comparison records non-operational; do not conflate HTTP errors with rejected fetch.
Remediation: catch per-monitor transport failures, record a failed check, continue remaining monitors, then persist; bounded timeout is a related design improvement but not required to demonstrate this defect.

S2 (P2, primary if CLI in audit scope): Removing a monitor makes garbage collection throw before saving any cleanup.
Evidence: src/cli/gcMonitors.js:67 iterates snapshot of old keys; :70 deletes absent monitor; :79 immediately dereferences stateMonitors.monitors[monitor].checks after deletion; :87-88 save is never reached. .github/workflows/deploy.yml runs yarn kv-gc after publishing.
Proof input: config IDs [A]; existing KV monitors {A:{checks:{}}, B:{checks:{oldDate:{}}}}. Iteration B deletes B, then reads undefined.checks -> TypeError, outer catch only logs. No cleaned state saved.
Remediation: continue/return after deletion or iterate remaining keys.

## Conditional accepted observation
S3 (P2/P3, secondary): Default every-minute successful cron writes one combined KV state per run, exceeding a Free namespace's 1,000 daily-write allowance: 60*24=1,440 writes/day, 440 above allowance, nominal exhaustion after 16h40 of successful scheduled writes (other traffic/offsets affect exact time). Two-minute cadence =720/day and is explicitly documented README:108-110. This is configuration/Free-plan conditional, not an undisclosed universal failure. Do not multiply writes by monitor count: all monitors share one state put. Paid plan does not have that daily cap.

## Safe / near-miss controls and unsupported claims
C1: index.js:31 registers processCronTrigger in event.waitUntil. helpers.js:12-13 returns setKV, setKV returns KV put promise, and cronTrigger.js:156 awaits it. No detached persistence task; no missing-await defect.
C2: notifications at :78/:89/:98 are registered with event.waitUntil. A notifier rejection does not itself imply the main KV put is never reached; distinguish from S1.
C3: pages/api/triggerCron.js has invocation commented out. Do not allege a public unauthenticated cron-trigger endpoint executes checks.
C4: checked-in config has 3 monitors. No established 50-subrequest exhaustion at this scale. Any larger-monitor warning must count actual fetch/KV/notification operations, paid/free plan and current limits; old README's historical 50 limit is not sufficient proof.
C5: KV eventual consistency is expressly acknowledged in README. Do not turn that into exact guaranteed 60-second lag, universal data loss, or a detached-write diagnosis.
C6: one-minute cron is not inherently above same-key 1 write/second limit; 1/60 < 1.
C7: no D1, Queue, R2, or Durable Object implementation in this scoped case; do not invent retries/delivery/transaction failures for unused services.

## Official platform references inspected (2026-11-06)
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/context/ : pending unregistered async work can be canceled; waitUntil registers work; origin fetch failure is caught in examples. Supports C1/C2 and distinction from S1.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/handlers/scheduled/ : scheduled waitUntil records asynchronous task outcome.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/platform/limits/ : regular KV Free 1,000 daily writes; same-key one/second. Supports conditional S3 and C6.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/concepts/how-kv-works/ : eventual consistency and visibility lag can exceed 60 seconds. Supports C5.

# Hidden author ground truth: web-tools D1 To-Do subsystem
DO NOT expose this file to audit variants. Independently selected after parent requested broader D1 coverage. No cfdoctor files or prior eval results read.
Pin: brucehart/web-tools@f1a09a2e80c9d3bc62786fe06409cad0b118a045.
Scope: src/todo.ts and shared session authentication, schema, HTTP/cookie helpers, entry routing and internal seed guard. Other tool APIs and Durable Object webhook subsystem are out of scope. Raw snapshot is deliberately not a complete runnable repo.
No target source or SQL was executed. These are source proofs, not live exploit claims.

## Significant confirmed defect
D1 (P2, primary): Expired session tokens remain valid server-side and can keep accessing the protected To-Do API.
Evidence: auth.ts:189 calculates seven-day expiresAt; :190 stores expires_at; migration 0001 defines expires_at as a plain TEXT column with no expiration trigger. getSessionUser at auth.ts:15 selects by s.token alone and never filters or reads expires_at; requireUser at :23-26 trusts any returned user; every To-Do route calls requireUser. internal-test.ts also issues a one-minute expiry without changing lookup logic.
Proof input: users contains user u; sessions contains token t for u with expiry yesterday; request supplies Cookie: wt_session=t. Token-only join still returns u. Browser Max-Age=604800 controls an honest browser's cookie retention, not validity of an explicitly replayed saved cookie. 7*24*60*60 = 604800 seconds; lifetime after that is unbounded by the shown lookup until row deletion, logout or external cleanup. Do not claim logout is broken: logout deletes its presented session token.
Remediation: enforce expiry in server lookup using one canonical comparable timestamp representation; stored value is RFC-style UTC string from toUTCString, so blindly comparing lexicographically or SQLite datetime(expires_at) without format validation is not a sound patch. Optional cleanup is not a replacement for enforcement.

## Confirmed lower-severity accepted observation
D2 (P2/P3, secondary): Concurrent toggle requests can lose one toggle.
Evidence: todo.ts:170 reads completed, :173 computes inverse locally, :174-176 writes a constant, with a separate awaited D1 call.
Interleaving: initial completed=0; A reads0, B reads0, A writes1, B writes1. Final1 after two successful toggles; serial toggles would end0. D1 single-statement atomicity does not make a multi-call JS read/modify/write atomic. It matters for simultaneous signed-in clients/retries; do not claim every toggle fails. Fix with database-side completed inversion in one UPDATE, owner-scoped WHERE, and returned updated state if supported. Replacing toggle with idempotent set-state can be a deliberate API redesign.
Do not require this lower-severity issue to count the case as detecting its primary defect.

## Safe / near-miss controls and unsupported claims
C1: Every To-Do route first calls requireUser and returns unauthorized Response. getTodo includes user_id in its bound WHERE. update/delete/toggle fetch owner and return403 for wrong user. Missing user_id in the final UPDATE/DELETE alone is not evidence of an exploitable owner bypass: IDs are immutable and no owner-transfer API is shown.
C2: Dynamic UPDATE at todo.ts:139 interpolates only hard-coded field assignments accumulated by explicit if branches; all values are supplied through .bind(...values). A malicious title remains a parameter; do not report SQL injection merely because updates.join is interpolated.
C3: env.DB is present as DB in wrangler.jsonc, and migrations define users/sessions/todos/category and owner indexes. No missing-binding or missing-category-column finding when all supplied migrations are applied.
C4: internal seed route requires POST plus a nonempty configured INTERNAL_TEST_KEY matching x-internal-key before ensureSchema or inserts. Config does not set that secret. No public unauthenticated seed/backdoor claim.
C5: cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; OAuth state has nonempty equality validation. D1 expiry omission does not imply missing OAuth state or missing cookie flags.
C6: each queried D1 statement is actually awaited through first/all/run. Bare prepare().bind() is not mistaken for execution.
C7: listTodos intentionally uses LIMIT500. Pagination/visibility above 500 can be a qualified secondary product limitation; no evidence it causes D1 result-limit failure for all users.
C8: no live deployed service was contacted. Database UUID, OAuth client ID and callback URL are public configuration identifiers, not credentials sufficient to access a DB or Google account.
C9: separate count-before-deleteCompleted may report stale deleted count under concurrency; at most a secondary correctness observation, not cross-user deletion (both statements bind userId).
C10: no Queue/R2 background path in this scope. Imported WebhookConnection reference is outside the scoped subsystem.

## Official platform references inspected (2026-11-06)
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/prepared-statements/ : bind supplies parameter values; first/all/run execute and retrieve rows. Supports SQL-injection safe control.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/ : D1 executes prepared SQL; auto-commit and batch transaction properties do not add a TTL to arbitrary expires_at columns or turn separate requests into one operation. Supports scope of D1/D2 reasoning.

# Independently authored evaluation notes: hookrelay

Repository: https://github.com/grunt-it/hookrelay
Pin: b92069bf3b618600cd5d40e8ddfb2854cc88e18d
Scope: complete tracked repository (21 files, 76,900 bytes), including all source, inline SQL schema, tests, config, README, package manifest and lockfile. No cfdoctor implementation, changes, prior report, or expected results were consulted. Source was read; target code was not executed. This ground truth is non-exhaustive. Findings describe conditional source defects, not observed production incidents.

## Significant source-grounded defects

H1 — Concurrent ingress is not idempotent (high confidence, P1/P2 depending on downstream effect).
Evidence: src/index.ts:31-35 and 52-54; README explicitly promises idempotent ingest; src/types.ts:3 states the invariant. The status get is separate from both puts and queue send. Two same-id requests may both read absence, both persist, and both enqueue. Conflicting same-id bodies can also overwrite the envelope each message later loads by id. This is a read/check/write race even before accounting for KV's eventual consistency. Queues' at-least-once semantics do not make ingress deduplication impossible, and do not excuse the explicitly promised guarantee.
Verification: with controlled in-memory KV/queue doubles, pause both gets before returning null, resume both requests, and assert two sends and possible envelope replacement. A local integration test should demonstrate that a strong unique claim prevents this. Fix with serialized per-id ownership/unique transactional insert and defined payload conflict handling; a KV read alone cannot claim uniqueness.
Boundary: duplicate webhook effects depend on destination deduplication. The webhook-id header is a useful receiver-side control; do not report guaranteed duplicate effects at every destination.

H2 — A rejected queue send leaves an id permanently accepted but never scheduled (high confidence, P1/P2).
Evidence: src/index.ts:52-54 creates event and queued status before awaiting DELIVERY_QUEUE.send; line 35 makes any subsequent same-id retry return early. If send rejects before acceptance, the request fails but leaves a queued status. Once that status is visible, retries never reach send. No outbox, reconciliation job or retry-pending state exists anywhere in the full snapshot.
Verification: make both KV puts succeed and send reject before accepting anything; retry same id after making KV visible. Observe status queued and zero successful sends. Fix with a durable recoverable outbox/state machine, atomic ownership plus enqueue recovery, or explicit retry of pending-unscheduled work. Merely deleting status on any send error is unsafe if send outcome is ambiguous.
Boundary: only a definite pre-accept failure proves no queue message; an ambiguous error requires reconciliation rather than assuming message loss.

H3 — A temporary KV envelope miss is explicitly acknowledged as final (high confidence, P1/P2).
Evidence: producer src/index.ts:52-54 writes event then sends only eventId; src/queue/consumer.ts:8-9 and 54-58 acknowledge a null envelope. There is no event TTL in the producer. Consumer execution at another location or a cached negative read can legally return null after the producer put succeeded. Explicit ack prevents future queue redelivery, so this path can silently lose an accepted event rather than letting visibility catch up.
Verification: inject a first consumer get that returns null followed by the actual event. Assert current code acks, makes no delivery and never retries. For runtime evidence, use an isolated local/runtime harness or controlled staging environment only when separately authorized; production frequency is not established here. Fix by making the queue envelope self-contained, using a strongly consistent envelope store, or retrying/reconciling missing data with bounded diagnostics rather than silently acking.
Boundary: a genuinely invalid envelope can merit quarantine; the source cannot distinguish that from a transient visibility miss.

H4 — The circuit's half-open state does not reserve the promised single probe (high confidence, P2).
Evidence: src/lib/rate-and-circuit.ts:60, 91-95 promises one probe but allows every call in half-open state. src/do/destination.ts:59-69 persists half-open at reservation time; consumer.ts:63-72 performs outbound delivery outside the object and reports result later. Thus after the first probe reserves and before its result arrives, subsequent reservations also pass (up to the independent token bucket). This is sequential state-machine behavior, not a speculative lost-update race. Multiple batches/consumers can have requests in flight at once.
Verification: start with open circuit past cooldown, call canAttempt and pass its state into a second call without recordSuccess/Failure. Both return allowed. At the DO boundary, hold the first outbound response while calling checkAndReserve again. Fix by representing a probe-in-flight state/lease, denying further reservations and recovering abandoned leases.
Boundary: token bucket still limits traffic; this does not mean the rate limiter is wholly absent. Existing tests cover opening, successful/failed probe, refill and capacity; they omit repeated half-open reservations.

## Intended controls and near misses

- Consumer awaits outcome classification, result recording and status writes, then acknowledges each successful/permanent item individually. A later unacked error should not reprocess earlier acked messages.
- 2xx delivery and permanent/transient classification are deliberate policy. Permanent errors are surfaced as failed, transient errors retry with capped backoff; wrangler.jsonc configures main queue max_retries=5, a DLQ, and its consumer. Missing DLQ is not a finding.
- A 10-second AbortController timeout is cleared in finally. HMAC signing includes timestamp/body and sends a stable webhook-id; verification and deduplication belong to the receiver.
- Destination is exported, bound, and created with new_sqlite_classes; the attempts table is created in blockConcurrencyWhile and INSERT values are parameterized.
- No multi-tenant auth, dashboard, or per-destination configuration is promised; README expressly limits this reference's scope. Missing those product choices is not a canonical defect. The placeholder KV namespace is documented setup, not an unexplained missing binding.
- No need to claim DO get/put counter races: storage gates may serialize these operations. H4 survives fully sequential execution.

## Hypotheses requiring evidence or product intent

- Gate denials call message.retry (consumer.ts:64-67); these retries count against max_retries even if no outbound HTTP attempt occurred. Under enough sustained competing traffic/circuit denial an event can reach DLQ without its own HTTP attempt. Verify with controlled saturation and inspect attempts. Whether finite admission retries are unacceptable needs a defined delivery SLO; do not infer it from the comment alone.
- Queue redelivery or failure after successful outbound send but before status/ack can duplicate deliveries. Stable webhook-id supports receiver deduplication; need destination contract/effect evidence before claiming financial or other concrete duplicate harm.
- Unbounded attempt-log/event retention could matter at scale; needs volume/retention requirements and limit evidence, not a mandatory finding.

## Official semantics checked on 2026-11-07

- https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/concepts/how-kv-works/ — KV can return stale values and negative lookups; it does not provide an atomic read/write transaction suitable for a uniqueness claim.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/batching-retries/ — explicit ack removes that item from retries; retry limits apply before DLQ/discard.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/ — queue delivery is at least once; receiver idempotency keys can reject duplicate effects.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/legacy-kv-storage-api/ — SQLite-backed DOs support the asynchronous KV storage API too. Do not flag their use as an incompatible storage backend.

## Evaluation guidance

Credit materially equivalent diagnoses with exact paths and conditional trigger/impact; do not require these titles or a fixed count. # Independently authored evaluation notes: workers-chat-demo

Repository: https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-chat-demo
Pin: dd32ce87617a9df6c614004d2fc2fb0628698121
Scope: complete tracked repository (8 files, 46,435 bytes), including both backend and browser client, README, manifest, workflow and config. No tests exist in this snapshot; none were omitted. No cfdoctor implementation, changes, prior report, or expected results were consulted. No target code execution, installer, deployed request, or account operation was performed. Ground truth is non-exhaustive.

This is a useful control-heavy example: most generic claims about absent validation, absent migration or lost named-session identity would be incorrect.

## Significant source-grounded conditional defect

C1 — Hibernation before initial user-info loses the pending client's history and roster (high confidence from source plus documented lifecycle, P2).
Evidence: src/chat.mjs:300-320 collects existing roster and last 100 stored messages into session.blockedMessages when accepting a socket. At accept time only limiterId is attached (302-303); name is attached on first message (347-352). Constructor recovery iterates live sockets but always sets blockedMessages to [] (222-239), deliberately declining to serialize it. The first user-info handler later flushes only that current array and sends ready (362-371), without rebuilding history or roster.
Trigger: a socket is accepted, client delays its first name message long enough for the room to hibernate, and then sends its name. Cloudflare preserves the socket but resets memory and reruns the constructor. The recovered socket has no name and an empty pending array, so it is declared ready without the history/roster assembled at connection time. Even a single persisted historic message and no other connected users suffice to show missing history. Reconstructing roster requires accounting for the other restored named sockets.
Impact: delayed or paused clients can silently miss the promised initial history and roster. This does not erase durable history for all clients.
Actionable verification: an isolated hibernation-capable runtime test should seed one historic message; accept a socket without sending user info; force/observe hibernation; send a valid name; compare frames with the same join without hibernation. Expected invariant is historical message before ready in both. A pure reconstruction harness can demonstrate dropped state, but actual hibernation timing is runtime evidence and has not been measured here.
Fix direction: persist a compact initialization phase/cursor and rebuild bounded history/roster after wake or defer collecting them until the user-info message; preserve initialization ordering around concurrent broadcasts. Do not put an arbitrarily growing blocked-message array into a size-limited attachment.

## Intended controls / safe near misses

- wrangler.toml:6-20 binds both exported classes and creates both via new_sqlite_classes. Async storage.get/put/list remains supported on SQLite-backed DOs; it is not a legacy-backend mismatch.
- Backend (not merely browser UI) rejects overlong room names, validates private IDs through idFromString, checks websocket Upgrade, limits names to 32 and messages to 256, and constructs message.name from server session state (chat.mjs:169-186, 261-263, 347-380).
- Named sessions survive normal hibernation: constructor restores each socket's attached name and limiter ID, reconstructs its RateLimiterClient, and maps it back to that socket (222-239). The conditional pending-client defect must not be generalized to all sockets forgetting identity.
- Private rooms intentionally use unguessable newUniqueId capabilities and anyone-with-link sharing (139-152). Lack of an account/password is not an access-control defect in that stated design.
- The client explicitly warns that names are unauthenticated and chat history is stored (chat.html:426-435). Identity spoofing of display names is a disclosed product choice.
- Client output uses innerText/createTextNode for names/messages (chat.html:411-418, 460-468); do not claim HTML execution from normal chat messages.
- The server stores history and loads a bounded latest 100 messages on ordinary initial connection. There is no Queues component here; no queue binding/DLQ expectation applies.
- RateLimiter is keyed by connecting IP across rooms. RateLimiterClient rejects within its local cooldown and reconnects a failed stub once. These are real controls, though not proof of an adversarial global bound.
- Error stack responses are expressly development/demo behavior. A production hardening suggestion may be reasonable; do not promote it to secret exfiltration without a concrete sensitive value/path.

## Hypotheses and limits

- checkLimit accepts one message before the remote limiter reply and each new socket gets a fresh local cooldown. Parallel new sockets or constructor rebuilding clients may overshoot global per-IP limits (chat.mjs:509-529). Measure accepted user-info/chat traffic over many connections under a controlled runtime and compare with an agreed bound. This author has not established an end-to-end adversarial abuse rate; no quantitative claim is ground truth.
- RateLimiter.nextAllowedTime exists only in memory (chat.mjs:466-488). Object eviction resets it. Whether that matters depends on the eviction interval relative to the owed cooldown. Verify lifecycle and sustained traffic before claiming unlimited sends.
- lastTimestamp resets in the ChatRoom constructor; a huge synthetic burst/future timestamp and subsequent recreation might cause key reuse. Ordinary hibernation exceeds a millisecond and no occurrence is shown. Treat as a hypothesis, not an established lost-history incident.
- Messages are broadcast before awaited storage.put; DO output-gate behavior matters. Do not assert a lost-durability bug merely from that source ordering.
- History retention and idle pre-name sockets are not explicitly bounded in persisted data/lifetime. Resource concerns require workload, limits, and intended retention policy.

- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/websockets/ — hibernation retains connected sockets, resets in-memory state and reruns the constructor; attachments can restore per-socket state.

# Independent author ground truth: reia-lfs-r2

Repository: https://github.com/Quaint-Studios/reia-lfs-cloudflare-worker
Pin: 2758c463e3b364f4cfb59010e2c25f0d544540eb
Prepared: 2026-11-07. Non-exhaustive ground truth. Author did not inspect cfdoctor, its changes, previous reports, or expected results. No target source, installer, tests, or deployed endpoint was executed.

## Scope and provenance
Complete four-file repository: worker.js, README.md, SECURITY.md, LICENSE; 22,457 bytes. No Wrangler, package manifest, schema, tests, build scripts, or migrations exist in the pinned tree; dashboard/manual environment binding is explicitly documented. Their absence is not evidence of a missing-file artifact.
manifest.json records SHA-256, Git blob SHA-1, byte length for every raw file; all matched upstream byte-for-byte. tree.json preserves complete upstream inventory.

## Primary significant defect
SC-R2-01 (P1/P2 depending impact model, source-proven integrity failure): upload accepts a syntactically valid OID but does not verify that uploaded bytes hash to that OID.
Evidence: worker.js:59 invokes isValidOid; implementation at 571 onward checks only length/hex characters. Authenticated upload at 376-386 checks that Content-Length exists, then directly calls LFS_BUCKET.put(lfsObjectPath(oid), request.body), with no sha256 option or computed hash comparison. lfsObjectPath builds the storage key from the supplied OID. Download uses that same key.
Consequence grounded in source: an allowed upload token can store arbitrary bytes under a SHA-256 content-addressed object name, and the unconditional PUT path can replace bytes already present at that key. This violates LFS content integrity and can make clients reject downloads or lose availability of a previously referenced object. This is an integrity problem within the intended authenticated upload capability, not an authentication bypass. No claim that the client silently accepts a mismatching SHA-256 object; Git LFS verification can detect it.
Remedy: validate the body against the expected SHA-256 before committing, or use the R2 put sha256 integrity option with a correctly encoded digest, and consider conditional create/idempotency to preserve existing objects. Merely checking HEAD before PUT does not close a concurrent replacement race.
Verification, not performed: in a local fake-R2/Workers fixture with an explicitly allowed synthetic token, choose an OID for known bytes A and PUT distinct bytes B with a valid Content-Length. Current source reaches put; fixed code must reject without changing existing A. Also verify A uploads successfully and an unauthorized request never reaches put.

## Secondary significant protocol defect
SC-R2-02 (P2, source-proven): Batch upload reports per-object 409 whenever the object already exists.
Evidence: worker.js:508-535, particularly 531. Git LFS Batch API specifies omitting actions for an object already held, so the client can treat it as successful deduplication. Code emits an object error instead.
Consequence: ordinary repeated pushes/retries/shared content encounter an object-level error even though the requested object is available. Exact client user-interface text and exit behavior require a client test; do not claim it was observed.
Remedy: return oid/size without actions or error when an existing verified object is present.
Verification, not performed: seed one object, perform a Batch upload for it using an allowed synthetic token, and require a successful object descriptor with no upload action or error; mix existing/missing objects and require the latter alone to receive upload actions.

## Intended controls and false-positive traps
- README explicitly promises public download. GET and public bucket download hrefs are intended, not unauthorized exposure.
- GET /generate signs a token but deliberately does not add tokenId to KV. Upload in both Batch and PUT requires a signed token AND a truthy KV allowlist entry (worker.js:368 and 443); calling /generate alone grants no write access.
- A token holder revoking their own token is the documented revoke capability; there is no evidence of cross-user arbitrary revocation without possession of the token.
- This server has one broad upload allowlist, not documented per-repository/per-object ownership. Do not invent a missing ownership requirement.
- Direct R2 streaming with request.body is an appropriate Workers pattern; no missing waitUntil since the PUT is awaited.
- R2/KV bindings and the secret are configured manually as README states. No Wrangler file exists upstream; do not allege an undeclared binding from a nonexistent config.
- Hex OID validation prevents slashes/backslashes and requires exactly 64 hex chars. Do not invent filesystem traversal.
- Constants containing service URLs are deployment customization context, not secret tokens.
- No automatic exp claim is made by README: generated tokens have no exp and KV controls revocation. Temporal policy should be a requirement question, not an automatic bypass finding.

## Hypotheses requiring runtime/environment evidence
KV allowlist revocation has eventual consistency; do not promise globally immediate invalidation. Exact revocation delay requires a dedicated fixture or platform evidence and is not measured here.
BUCKET_URL assumes a publicly reachable bucket domain; deployment config is unavailable, so broken bucket routing is only a configuration hypothesis.
Malformed Basic input and non-string/missing OIDs may throw and be translated to 500; reproduce in a local harness before presenting exact responses. They do not bypass allowlist/signature checks.
No billing, denial-of-service scale, deployed incident, or account compromise is demonstrated.

## Primary official references checked 2026-11-07
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/workers/workers-api-reference/ — awaited put accepts request streams; R2PutOptions exposes sha256 integrity checking and onlyIf conditions.
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/main/docs/api/batch.md — hash_algo defaults to sha256; an existing upload object should omit actions and be considered already present.
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/main/docs/api/basic-transfers.md — upload uses bytes and the returned action URL; optional verify actions do not require skipping server integrity checks.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/concepts/how-kv-works/ — eventual consistency qualifications.
